cfyWvJdsDRI.title: Mock Interview with Shawn McGrath
cfyWvJdsDRI.summary: A live mock programmer interview in which Casey Muratori interviews game developer Shawn McGrath using a less confrontational format devised by Chris Hecker. It gets deep into technical details while showing how the candidate actually thinks and works.
cfyWvJdsDRI.why: HN cites it as the example of a better alternative to whiteboard and fizzbuzz-style interviews.

quote.text: please watch this alternative method of interviewing

rQmqVVmMB3k.title: The $100 Billion Dollar Ingredient making your Food Toxic
rQmqVVmMB3k.summary: A What I've Learned video arguing that industrial seed and vegetable oils have displaced saturated fats and harmed health. It covers the history of vegetable oils, the American Heart Association's role, and rising consumption.
rQmqVVmMB3k.why: HN commenters recommend it as an accessible summary of the case against seed oils, and some say it changed what fats they cook with.

quote.text: one of the most important ones imo being the one on seed oils

smStEPSRKBs.title: Atari's Quadrascan Explained
smStEPSRKBs.summary: Retro Game Mechanics Explained dissects how Atari's Quadrascan vector displays and vector generator hardware drew games like Asteroids and Tempest.
smStEPSRKBs.why: Recommended whenever Atari vector games come up as an excellent, deep technical explanation of how they worked.

quote.text: There’s an excellent video by Retro Game Mechanics Explained on how they work

85ZCTuekjGA.title: Building a 6800 CPU on an FPGA with nMigen (part 1)
85ZCTuekjGA.summary: The first part of Robert Baruch's series on building a 6800 CPU on an FPGA with nMigen, a Python-based hardware description language. It introduces the HDL while implementing a simpler 6800 core.
85ZCTuekjGA.why: HN recommends the series as a practical introduction to nMigen and formal verification for CPU design.

quote.text: I can only recommend these Youtube series, where nMigen is used to build a full 6800 CPU

SfsCniN7Nsc.title: The Suburbs Are Bleeding America Dry | Climate Town (feat. @NotJustBikes)
SfsCniN7Nsc.summary: A snarky, comedic video essay from Climate Town, with a guest appearance by Not Just Bikes, arguing that American suburban sprawl and single-family zoning are financially and environmentally unsustainable. It covers how zoning rules shape housing and what viewers can do locally, such as attending zoning meetings.
SfsCniN7Nsc.why: HN commenters cite it as an entertaining but well-sourced explainer on US zoning and housing costs whenever those topics come up.

quote.text: A funny, yet very well researched video on that exact same topic of Zoning nonsense. Entertaining AND informative.

zmCTmgavkrQ.title: The Fermi Paradox: Dark Forest Theory
zmCTmgavkrQ.summary: Isaac Arthur examines the Dark Forest theory, Cixin Liu's proposed solution to the Fermi Paradox in which civilizations stay silent and may destroy any that reveal themselves. He tests the theory's underlying assumptions and arguments.
zmCTmgavkrQ.why: HN commenters point to it as a well-argued rebuttal of Dark Forest axioms, and recommend his wider Fermi Paradox series.

quote.text: His entire library on the Fermi Paradox is worth watching.

LwicN2u6Dro.title: "Liberating the Smalltalk lurking in C and Unix" by Stephen Kell
LwicN2u6Dro.summary: Stephen Kell's Strange Loop talk argues that C and Unix already contain Smalltalk-like dynamism and introspection that can be exposed. He presents his liballocs research on bridging dynamic and compiled languages.
LwicN2u6Dro.why: HN commenters recommend it in Smalltalk and Unix threads as a demonstration of runtime dynamism hiding in native binaries and shared libraries.
LwicN2u6Dro.topic: dynamic features in c and unix

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: there's a great video of one of his talks

M_VuXVErD6E.title: Design Your Own Keyboard!
M_VuXVErD6E.summary: Ben Vallack walks through designing a custom keyboard PCB from scratch using Ergogen and KiCad, ending with a gerber file ready to order from a PCB fabricator. The example is a split keyboard.
M_VuXVErD6E.why: HN recommends it as a thorough, general walkthrough of the steps in designing your own keyboard.

quote.text: It's targeting a split keyboard, but I think it details the general steps involved pretty well.

P_fHJIYENdI.title: AlphaFold - The Most Useful Thing AI Has Ever Done
P_fHJIYENdI.summary: A Veritasium video on AlphaFold, DeepMind's protein structure prediction system, and the protein design work it enabled. It features interviews with John Jumper and with David Baker's protein design group and explains why predicting protein folding matters.
P_fHJIYENdI.why: HN points to it as an accessible explainer of AlphaFold and as an example of narrow, specialized ML delivering real scientific breakthroughs.

quote.text: To learn more about AlphaFold and its importance, I would recommend the Veritasium video[0]

SEwTjZvy8vw.title: 2023 LLVM Dev Mtg - Mojo 🔥: A system programming language for heterogenous computing
SEwTjZvy8vw.summary: A 2023 LLVM Developers' Meeting keynote by Abdul Dakkak, Chris Lattner and Jeff Niu introducing Mojo, a Python-family systems language built on MLIR and LLVM for heterogeneous computing.
SEwTjZvy8vw.why: HN points to it as the best deep dive into Mojo's design, including MLIR use and SIMD-first scalars.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: this video totally changed my view

Ze2pc6NwsHQ.title: Optimizing Workspace for Productivity, Focus, & Creativity
Ze2pc6NwsHQ.summary: A Huberman Lab episode on setting up a workspace for productivity, focus and creativity, covering light, posture, movement and sound. It touches on ideas like ceiling height and the effect of screens on the brain.
Ze2pc6NwsHQ.why: Pointed to when people ask for science-based ways to boost concentration or arrange a home office.

Olj8arvfYj4.title: Why the US Drops 14.7 Million Worms On Panama Every Week
Olj8arvfYj4.summary: A Half as Interesting explainer on the US program that drops millions of sterile screwworm flies over Panama every week to keep the parasite out of North America.
Olj8arvfYj4.why: Cited in screwworm threads as a short description of the sterile-insect barrier system that worked for decades.

quote.text: Here's a video describing the system that fell apart which had been working for a long time

AA4IWd3Svm0.title: Virtuo Vivo™ live scanning at IDS 2019
AA4IWd3Svm0.summary: A short live demo of Dental Wings' Virtuo Vivo intraoral scanner at IDS 2019. It shows a fast color scan with a small, lightweight handpiece.
AA4IWd3Svm0.why: Posted by an employee as a showcase of a polished desktop application, with a JavaFX UI, built by a small team.

quote.text: Very impressive indeed. Looks effortless and natural

BZoKfap4g4w.title: The magic washing machine | Hans Rosling
BZoKfap4g4w.summary: Hans Rosling makes the case that the washing machine was the greatest invention of the industrial revolution. Using Gapminder graphics, he shows how electricity and economic growth free up time for reading and learning.
BZoKfap4g4w.why: Referenced when discussing how much time household technology saved families and how heavy housework used to be.

quote.text: He essentially made the case that the washing machine made a huge difference in the history of the world

KM6X2MEl7R8.title: warner music claimed my video for defending their copyright in a lawsuit they lost the copyright for

XQQYbKT_rMg.title: Star Trek Economy
